cells.tense: What you carried through a hard change is steady now, and you stand beside it at the table.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: At the next exchange with somebody close, hand over what you've been keeping back and accept what you've been leaving untaken, both in the same stretch of talking.
cells.core:
What you carried through a hard change is standing now — a house, a practice, a way you keep yourself well. Around the people close to you, you can weigh what goes out against what comes back without a ledger running in your head. When someone hands you their part, you take it cleanly. When you hand yours over, you don't go quiet about the size of it.

Where this gets uneasy is a trade between you that sits unconfirmed, so the same figure gets counted again by both sides.

A small proof of the other way, this week. Hand over the thing you've been keeping back — the favour, the truth, the piece of yourself — and accept the thing you've been leaving untaken. Both directions happen in the same stretch of talking, so nothing is left owed. Fairness stays a flow rather than a score kept in a drawer.
cells.sheetLine: What you kept through the change can move between you now.
cells.verb: Holding what change produced before it goes out into the world
cells.place: Where what's out of proportion gets set level between people

cells.tense: You will have things held so tightly that no hand, including yours, can move them.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Before you settle the next thing about someone you love, let yourself be pulled toward what they might be feeling and stay there a while — decide nothing while it pulls.
cells.core:
Among the people close to you, keeping has become gripping. A thing built through change is still needing to be held, and you're holding it before the moment it's for — bracing for a loss that hasn't happened, settling who owes what before the feeling has finished being felt. From outside it looks like care. From inside it is a fist. The people close to you have stopped putting things on the table because the table keeps getting cleared.

Let the pull run first. Let yourself be drawn toward what the other person might be feeling before you choose anything — before you make the numbers even, before you decide what's fair. Not forever. Just long enough that the feeling has a shape you didn't give it. What you're carrying can wait, and it will still be there afterwards, with less to defend.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping what needs holding before it needs holding.
cells.verb: Holding what change produced before it goes out into the world
cells.place: Where what's out of proportion gets set level between people

cells.tense: You were left holding something after a change, and you have not moved since.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Take the direction you chose after the change, and next time something tugs you off it, hold that heading once, without explaining or re-arguing it.
cells.core:
Back when things changed, something needed holding — a place, a person, a version of the week — and you took the job. The job stayed, and you kept standing at the door it came through. What shifted back then still has your weight on it. Fairness between you and other people has gone quiet, because keeping a thing still isn't the same as being near anyone.

There is a direction you chose once, in the middle of all that, and it still makes sense. Stand in it again. The next time something tugs you off it — a request, a doubt, an old obligation — hold that heading once and see what happens. Not a campaign. One push refused. Movement comes back into the space where a held thing was sitting, and the held thing turns out to be lighter than standing still.
cells.sheetLine: You're still guarding a door the change already closed.
cells.verb: Holding what change produced before it goes out into the world
cells.place: Where what's out of proportion gets set level between people

cells.tense: The arrangement around you stays level, and every day the leveling looks like somebody else's doing.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Where a small thing needs deciding among you and the others, settle it before the day is out and follow through, with no talk about whose idea it was.
cells.core:
Among the people in your day-to-day, things stay even — a word shifted here, a share handed over there — and if someone asked how, you would say you stayed out of it. The evenness has a keeper. It is kept daily, without an announcement, by someone who does not count themselves as a maker of it. What you built after a hard change is probably what does it: a way of running the week, a habit of fairness, a small structure that somebody had to set.

Let the call show by carrying it. Where a small thing needs deciding among you and the others — who takes the shift, where the money goes, which rule holds — settle it and follow through, with no speech about whose idea it was. You'll watch the leveling happen from inside, and the person who made the arrangement tends to be the last to see it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep things fair and call it none of your doing.
cells.verb: Holding what change produced before it goes out into the world
cells.place: Where what's out of proportion gets set level between people

attempts.check: The draft risks saying the person is 'hoarding' when the record only says a thing produced by change needs holding before it is shared — the reader could object that nothing was won, no clearing happened, and I'd have nothing left to use. The Balanced ask survives being wrong because trading a keep for a release inside a real arrangement teaches the shape of fair exchange whatever the state; the Unacknowledged risk is naming the group's story as the person's authorship when they may genuinely be a bystander, so I've said only that the keeping has a keeper. The sentence that serves me more than them was any line about 'the harvest' — struck; plain facts of a table and a word stand in.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is that a thing 'built through change' exists to be kept — the record says something produced by change needs holding, but the person may not recognise any such thing, so every cell keeps the object optional and lets them supply it. The reader could reasonably object that the balanced cell assumes an exchange already running with somebody close; if that's wrong, the ask still teaches the shape of one trade and costs nothing. The sentence that serves me more than them was any line about 'the harvest' or 'what the clearing created' — struck; the asks and cores now stand on plain acts a camera could see. The four asks open on hand, let, hold, decide, so the shapes differ.
